title: Daniel in Babylon: The Furnace, the Wall and the Lions | Bible Stories for Sleep
description:
Settle in, dim the lights, and listen to the story of Daniel: a young man carried from Jerusalem to Babylon, four friends at a foreign king's table, Nebuchadnezzar's dream of a great statue and a small stone, three friends who would not bow before the golden image, a fourth figure walking in the fiery furnace, a great tree cut down and a proud king humbled, the hand that wrote on the wall beside the lamp, an open window toward Jerusalem, a long night in the lions' den, and an old man's last vision beside a great river. A calm, slow-paced retelling of the book of Daniel for sleep, with the key passages read from scripture itself.

🌙 Best with a low volume and the screen dimmed. You can let it play through the night.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Welcome, and a City by the River
14:41 Four Young Men and the King's Table
30:43 A Dream in the Night
45:31 The Statue and the Stone
58:58 The Golden Image on the Plain
1:11:30 The Fourth Man in the Fire
1:23:01 The Great Tree and the Humbled King
1:37:08 The Hand by the Lamp
1:52:01 An Open Window Toward Jerusalem
2:03:11 The Night in the Lions' Den
2:14:59 Seventy Years, and a Prayer at Evening
2:31:01 By the Great River, and Goodnight

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
The narration is AI-generated (an open-source text-to-speech voice) and is disclosed as altered or synthetic content. The retelling was written for this channel and checked against the text of Daniel, with background from Jeremiah, 2 Kings, Psalm 137 and Ezra 1. Historical notes (Nebuchadnezzar II, the Ishtar Gate, Belshazzar and Nabonidus, the fall of Babylon in 539 BC, the Cyrus Cylinder) follow standard museum and reference sources, and open questions (the date of the book, Darius the Mede) are mentioned honestly. Nothing is invented and no sermon is added.

SCRIPTURE
Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (public domain), lightly adapted for reading aloud: the divine name is rendered as "the Lord". Passages read: Daniel 1 to 7, 9, 10 and 12; Psalm 137:1-4; Jeremiah 29:4-11; Ezra 1:1-3; Numbers 6:24-26.

IMAGES
Public-domain artworks, engravings and photographs from Wikimedia Commons and museum collections, including works by David Roberts, James Tissot, Rembrandt, Julius Schnorr von Carolsfeld, Eduard Bendemann, Gustave Doré, John Martin, Master of the Feast of Belshazzar, Briton Rivière, David Teniers the Younger. Full list of file pages on request in the comments.

This video is for rest and reflection. It is not medical advice. If you have trouble sleeping regularly, please talk to a doctor.

title: Ruth and Esther: Two Women of Quiet Courage | Bible Stories for Sleep
description:
Settle in, dim the lights, and listen to two of the Bible's shortest and gentlest books. First, the story of Ruth: a famine in Bethlehem, a family in Moab, a grieving widow named Naomi, and a young Moabite woman who said, where you go, I will go. Barley fields at harvest time, a kind landowner named Boaz, a quiet night on the threshing floor, and a child named Obed, the grandfather of King David. Then, the story of Esther: the great palace at Susa, an orphan girl who became queen of Persia, her cousin Mordecai, the proud Haman and the casting of the lot, the words for such a time as this, the golden scepter, and a night when the king could not sleep. A calm, slow-paced retelling for sleep, with the whole book of Ruth and much of Esther read from scripture itself.

🌙 Best with a low volume and the screen dimmed. You can let it play through the night.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Welcome, and a Famine in Bethlehem
11:07 The Road Back, and Where You Go, I Will Go
22:39 Gleaning in the Barley Field
34:14 An Evening Conversation, and a Long Harvest
43:08 A Night on the Threshing Floor
54:22 At the Town Gate, and a Child Named Obed
1:09:10 A Long Road East, and the Palace at Susa
1:23:42 A Young Woman Named Hadassah
1:36:04 Haman, and the Casting of the Lot
1:47:39 For Such a Time as This
1:58:28 The Golden Scepter, and a Night Without Sleep
2:14:37 The Queen Speaks, a Day of Rest, and Goodnight

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
The narration is AI-generated (an open-source text-to-speech voice) and is disclosed as altered or synthetic content. The retelling was written for this channel and checked against the text of Ruth and Esther. Background notes (gleaning in the law of Leviticus 19 and Deuteronomy 24, the kinsman-redeemer, the town gate, Susa and the Persian Empire, Ahasuerus often identified with Xerxes I, the feast of Purim) follow standard reference sources, and open questions are mentioned honestly. Nothing is invented and no sermon is added. The hard passage in Esther 9 is summarized briefly rather than read.

Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (public domain), lightly adapted for reading aloud: the divine name is rendered as "the Lord". Passages read: Ruth 1 to 4 (the whole book); Esther 1:1-22; 2:5-23; 3:1-15; 4:4-17; 5:1-14; 6:1-14; 7:1-10; 8:3-8, 15-17; 9:20-22; 10:1-3.

title: The Life of David: Shepherd, Poet and King | Bible Stories for Sleep
description:
Settle in, dim the lights, and listen to the life of David: a shepherd boy anointed in Bethlehem, a harp in King Saul's house, five smooth stones in the valley of Elah, a friendship with Jonathan, years of hiding in the caves of the wilderness, a crown in Hebron and a city on a hill, a great wrong and a prophet's story, the grief of a father for Absalom, and an old king's last song. A calm, slow-paced retelling of 1 and 2 Samuel and the opening of 1 Kings for sleep, with the key passages and Psalms read from scripture itself.

🌙 Best with a low volume and the screen dimmed. You can let it play through the night.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Welcome, and a Boy with the Sheep
13:46 A Harp in the King's House
23:47 The Valley of Elah
37:48 Jonathan, and a Song That Went Wrong
51:00 A Fugitive in the Wilderness
1:01:32 The Cave at En Gedi, and a Wise Woman
1:14:50 A Spear, a Water Jar, and the Mountains of Gilboa
1:28:09 A King in Hebron, and a City on a Hill
1:38:29 Dancing Before the Ark, and a Promise of a House
1:49:08 A Rooftop in the Evening, and a Prophet's Story
2:01:59 Absalom, and the Road Up the Mount of Olives
2:14:23 Last Words, a Song, and Goodnight

ABOUT THIS VIDEO
The narration is AI-generated (an open-source text-to-speech voice) and is disclosed as altered or synthetic content. The retelling was written for this channel and checked against the text of 1 and 2 Samuel and 1 Kings. Where the text is hard (the death of Saul, David and Bathsheba, the rebellion of Absalom), the narration stays honest and gentle; nothing is invented and no sermon is added.

SCRIPTURE
Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (public domain), lightly adapted for reading aloud: the divine name is rendered as "the Lord". Passages read: 1 Samuel 16 to 30, 2 Samuel 1 to 23, 1 Kings 2, and Psalms 3, 23, 51 and 57.

Tapestry and painting details include the "David and Bathsheba" tapestries (Musée national de la Renaissance, Écouen) and engravings from the Rijksmuseum collection.
